Attributes, aliases and conversion

Source: vignettes/attributes.Rmd
attributes.Rmd

What problem does this solve?

Energy models, statistics and inventories carve fuels into categories, and every source carves differently: the IPCC lists fifty-odd fuels, a model has a handful of commodity codes, a chart wants a dozen colours. The numbers that turn one quantity into another – a net calorific value in GJ/t, a CO2 factor in kg/TJ – are published per category, for some categories, and the category a figure is published for is rarely the one the data is keyed by.

A nested scale keeps such numbers as attributes: values that belong to a member at whatever level they are published, resolved down the hierarchy when a finer member has none of its own, and applied row by row. The same mechanism serves any dimension – an area per region, an hour count per time slice – but fuels are where it earns its keep, so this vignette works on the shipped fuel taxonomy.

The shipped taxonomy

carriers is the fuel taxonomy of the energypal palettes, frozen as a definition file: 71 fuels under 17 carriers under 8 groups.

carriers <- read_scale("carriers")
carriers
#> NestedScale: carriers
#> Description: Energy carriers: fuels and energy vectors with subtypes, from energypal's carriers palette (IPCC 2006 / IEA classifications) 
#> Frames (3, coarsest first):
#>   - group (8)
#>     - carrier (17)
#>       - fuel (71)
#> Atoms: 71
#> Attributes: lhv, ef_co2 (sources: IPCC2006) -- 26 at fuel
#> Aliases: 136 (energypal, commodity)
#> Source: energypal carriers.yml
scale_units(carriers, "carrier")
#>  [1] "FossilCoal"          "FossilOil"           "FossilGas"          
#>  [4] "Bioenergy"           "Hydro"               "Wind"               
#>  [7] "Solar"               "Geothermal"          "OtherRenewables"    
#> [10] "Nuclear"             "Electricity"         "Heat"               
#> [13] "Hydrogen"            "HydrogenDerivatives" "SyntheticFuels"     
#> [16] "Storage"             "Other"
scale_children(carriers, "carrier", "FossilCoal")
#> [1] "Anthracite"      "Bituminous"      "SubBituminous"   "Lignite"        
#> [5] "Coke"            "OtherFossilCoal"

Codes repeat across frames (Nuclear is a group and the carrier inside it), so every lookup names its frame.

It carries the IPCC 2006 default net calorific values and CO2 factors for the fuels whose definition matches an IPCC fuel. Where there is no match, there is no number – the package never fills one in:

lhv <- scale_attributes(carriers, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
lhv[!is.na(lhv$value), c("unit", "value", "unit_of_measure", "source")]
#>                 unit value unit_of_measure   source
#> 1         Anthracite  26.7            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 2         Bituminous  25.8            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 3      SubBituminous  18.9            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 4            Lignite  11.9            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 5               Coke  28.2            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 7              Crude  42.3            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 8    ResidualFuelOil  40.4            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 9  DistillateFuelOil  43.0            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 10     MotorGasoline  44.3            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 11           JetFuel  44.1            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 12           LPG_NGL  47.3            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 14        NaturalGas  48.0            GJ/t IPCC2006
#> 23         Biodiesel  27.0            GJ/t IPCC2006

Attributes are not weights

A weight says how big an atom is: hours in a time slice, area of a region, consumption of a fuel. Weights drive aggregation (weighted_mean up) and disaggregation (sum split down). They are declared on the leaftable and sum over the scale.

A calorific value is none of those things. It is a conversion factor: it turns a tonne of this fuel into gigajoules, row by row, and summing it over fuels is meaningless. So a scale keeps attributes in a separate table, keyed by (frame, unit), and consumes them only in convert_scale(). The constructor promotes numeric leaftable columns to weights; a calorific value passed as a column would become a weight and be summed. Pass it as attributes=.

Averaging an attribute over a fuel mix is a legitimate aggregation – the mean calorific value of “coal” given how much of each coal is burnt. That is an ordinary recast of a resolved attribute with the weighted_mean rule, and the weight is where weights live: on the scale, as the consumption of each fuel.

coal <- filter_scale(carriers, "carrier", "FossilCoal")
lt <- scale_leaftable(coal)
lt$tj <- c(100, 300, 50, 400, 20, 0)
mix <- scale_from_leaftable(
  lt, frames = c("group", "carrier", "fuel"), key = "fuel",
  attributes = scale_attributes(coal), name = "mix"
)
lhv_coal <- scale_attributes(mix, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
recast_scale(
  data.frame(fuel = lhv_coal$unit, lhv = lhv_coal$value), mix,
  source = "fuel", target = "carrier", rule = "weighted_mean", weight = "tj"
)
#>      carrier lhv
#> 1 FossilCoal  NA

(filter_scale() keeps only the attribute rows of the surviving members, so the subset’s table is exactly what the new scale may take.)

Attributes live at any frame, and resolve by nearest ancestor

A value may be stored on a fuel, on a carrier or on a group. When a fuel has no value of its own, scale_attributes() walks to the nearest coarser frame that holds one and reports where the value came from. The shipped data stores everything at the fuel level; a carrier-level figure from another source fills the gaps below it without touching the fuels that have their own:

gas <- attach_attributes_scale(
  carriers,
  data.frame(frame = "carrier", unit = "FossilGas", attribute = "lhv",
             kind = "property", value = 46, unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "example"
)
res <- scale_attributes(gas, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
res[res$unit %in% scale_children(gas, "carrier", "FossilGas"),
    c("unit", "value", "source", "origin_frame", "origin_unit")]
#>              unit value   source origin_frame origin_unit
#> 14     NaturalGas    48 IPCC2006         fuel  NaturalGas
#> 15       ShaleGas    46  example      carrier   FossilGas
#> 16       TightGas    46  example      carrier   FossilGas
#> 17            LNG    46  example      carrier   FossilGas
#> 18  AssociatedGas    46  example      carrier   FossilGas
#> 19 OtherFossilGas    46  example      carrier   FossilGas

NaturalGas keeps its IPCC value; its siblings inherit the carrier’s. Nothing is guessed from a sibling or an average.

Two situations are refused rather than resolved:

  • Ambiguity across a cross-cutting frame. When the walk reaches a frame where the member has several ancestors and one of them holds the attribute, it cannot pick one and errors; if none does, it continues to the next coarser frame. vignette("anatomy") builds a scale with such a frame.
  • Several sources. Two sources publishing the same attribute for the same member is an error unless source= chooses. The walk stays within the chosen source: a source that lacks a fuel reports NA rather than borrowing another’s figure.
two <- attach_attributes_scale(
  carriers,
  data.frame(frame = "fuel", unit = "Anthracite", attribute = "lhv",
             kind = "property", value = 27.5, unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "other"
)
scale_attributes(two, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
#> Error:
#> ! `lhv` for `Anthracite` at frame `fuel` is published by several sources (IPCC2006, other); pass `source=`
other <- scale_attributes(two, "lhv", frame = "fuel", source = "other")
other[!is.na(other$value), c("unit", "value", "source")]
#>         unit value source
#> 1 Anthracite  27.5  other

Sources and provenance

Every attribute row names its source and unit_of_measure. Attaching never overwrites: a row with the same (frame, unit, attribute, source) is an error, so the way to add a better number is to attach it under its own source name and select it. Every attribute name carries a kind (SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS): a property is an invertible ratio, a factor converts one way only. Any attribute name is accepted.

Mass to energy, with the calorific value

convert_scale() multiplies each row by the attribute resolved for its fuel. lhv is stored in GJ/t, so the direction is tonnes to gigajoules; the result reports which factor was applied and where it came from.

use <- data.frame(
  fuel = c("Anthracite", "Lignite", "NaturalGas", "Biodiesel"),
  kt   = c(120, 900, 0, 15)
)
use$t <- use$kt * 1e3                 # kt -> t: no prefix arithmetic is done
energy <- convert_scale(use[c("fuel", "t")], carriers, "lhv",
                        from_unit = "t", to_unit = "GJ")
energy
#>         fuel        t  lhv lhv.origin_frame
#> 1 Anthracite  3204000 26.7             fuel
#> 2    Lignite 10710000 11.9             fuel
#> 3 NaturalGas        0 48.0             fuel
#> 4  Biodiesel   405000 27.0             fuel

A fuel without a value is an error, not a silent zero. Pass na_action = "keep" to carry NA instead. A property converts both ways:

convert_scale(energy[c("fuel", "t")], carriers, "lhv",
              from_unit = "GJ", to_unit = "t")
#>         fuel      t  lhv lhv.origin_frame
#> 1 Anthracite 120000 26.7             fuel
#> 2    Lignite 900000 11.9             fuel
#> 3 NaturalGas      0 48.0             fuel
#> 4  Biodiesel  15000 27.0             fuel

Aggregate to carriers

Aggregation is a recast with an explicit rule; sum conserves the total. Register the rule once per column, or pass rule= each time.

One decision has to be stated. The table reports four fuels against a taxonomy of 71. By default an absent fuel is unknown, and every carrier that contains one aggregates to NA with a warning – the safe reading for incomplete data. Fuel statistics usually mean the other thing, that an unreported fuel was not used, and missing_sources = "ignore" says so.

tj <- data.frame(fuel = energy$fuel, tj = energy$t / 1e3)   # GJ -> TJ
register_scale_rule("tj", "sum")
by_carrier <- recast_scale(tj, carriers, source = "fuel", target = "carrier",
                           missing_sources = "ignore")
#> Warning: 67 source unit(s) present in the scale but missing from the data (e.g.
#> Ammonia, AssociatedGas, Battery, ... (67 total)); produced NAs
by_carrier[by_carrier$tj > 0, ]
#>          carrier    tj
#> 1     FossilCoal 13914
#> NA          <NA>    NA
#> 4      Bioenergy   405
#> NA.1        <NA>    NA
#> NA.2        <NA>    NA
#> NA.3        <NA>    NA
#> NA.4        <NA>    NA
#> NA.5        <NA>    NA
#> NA.6        <NA>    NA
#> NA.7        <NA>    NA
#> NA.8        <NA>    NA
#> NA.9        <NA>    NA
#> NA.10       <NA>    NA
#> NA.11       <NA>    NA
#> NA.12       <NA>    NA
#> NA.13       <NA>    NA
sum(by_carrier$tj, na.rm = TRUE) == sum(tj$tj)
#> [1] TRUE

Emissions, one-way

An emission factor converts energy to CO2 and nothing else: convert_scale() refuses the inverse because ef_co2 is stored with kind factor, not property.

co2 <- convert_scale(tj, carriers, "ef_co2", from_unit = "TJ", to_unit = "kg")
names(co2)[names(co2) == "tj"] <- "co2_kg"
co2
#>         fuel     co2_kg ef_co2 ef_co2.origin_frame
#> 1 Anthracite  314953200  98300                fuel
#> 2    Lignite 1081710000 101000                fuel
#> 3 NaturalGas          0  56100                fuel
#> 4  Biodiesel   28674000  70800                fuel
convert_scale(tj, carriers, "ef_co2", from_unit = "kg", to_unit = "TJ")
#> Error:
#> ! `ef_co2` converts TJ -> kg only; the inverse is refused because it is a factor, not a property (see SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS)

Where the numbers come from

Every IPCC row ships, with its mapping status, so the choice to attach a figure to a fuel is inspectable:

ipcc <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "ipcc2006_fuel_defaults.csv",
                             package = "nestedscales"))
table(ipcc$attribute, ipcc$mapping_status)
#>         
#>          mapped review unmapped
#>   ef_co2     16     15       22
#>   lhv        16     15       22
review <- ipcc[ipcc$mapping_status == "review" & ipcc$attribute == "lhv", ]
review[c("ipcc_fuel", "unit", "value")]
#>                                   ipcc_fuel           unit value
#> 9                         Aviation Gasoline                 44.3
#> 11                             Jet Gasoline                 44.3
#> 15                           Other Kerosene                 43.8
#> 43                 Other Petroleum Products OtherFossilOil  40.2
#> 77  Municipal Wastes (non-biomass fraction)          Waste  10.0
#> 79                        Industrial Wastes          Waste    NA
#> 85                          Wood/Wood Waste   SolidBiomass  15.6
#> 89              Other Primary Solid Biomass   SolidBiomass  11.6
#> 91                                 Charcoal   SolidBiomass  29.5
#> 93                              Biogasoline        Ethanol  27.0
#> 97                    Other Liquid Biofuels OtherBioenergy  27.4
#> 99                             Landfill Gas         Biogas  50.4
#> 101                              Sludge Gas         Biogas  50.4
#> 103                            Other Biogas         Biogas  50.4
#> 105     Municipal Wastes (biomass fraction)          Waste  11.6

A different source – a country-specific calorific value, a plant-level measurement – is attached under its own source and chosen with source= when reading; nothing is overwritten.

mine <- attach_attributes_scale(
  carriers,
  data.frame(frame = "fuel", unit = "Lignite", attribute = "lhv",
             kind = "property", value = 8.4, unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "plant"
)
plant <- scale_attributes(mine, "lhv", frame = "fuel", source = "plant")
plant[!is.na(plant$value), c("unit", "value", "source")]
#>      unit value source
#> 4 Lignite   8.4  plant

Model commodity codes

Models key fuels by short codes. scale_match() resolves them through the alias table, exactly and case-insensitively, first against member names and then against aliases, and reports ambiguity instead of guessing. There is no fuzzy or substring stage: a model input is not the place for a near miss.

scale_match(carriers, c("GAS", "LIG", "ELC", "Hydrogen"))
#>      label   frame        unit    method                      candidates
#> 1      GAS carrier   FossilGas     alias                            <NA>
#> 2      LIG    fuel     Lignite     alias                            <NA>
#> 3      ELC carrier Electricity     alias                            <NA>
#> 4 Hydrogen    <NA>        <NA> ambiguous carrier/Hydrogen; fuel/Hydrogen
scale_match(carriers, "Hydrogen", frame = "carrier")
#>      label   frame     unit method candidates
#> 1 Hydrogen carrier Hydrogen  exact       <NA>

Attaching the hierarchy, and colours

A table keyed by fuel gets its carrier and group with one join; the added columns are prefixed by the scale’s name, so a second scale on the same table never collides with the first.

join_scale(use[c("fuel", "kt")], carriers, frame = "fuel", attach = TRUE)
#>         fuel  kt carriers.group carriers.carrier   carriers
#> 1 Anthracite 120    FossilFuels       FossilCoal Anthracite
#> 2    Lignite 900    FossilFuels       FossilCoal    Lignite
#> 3 NaturalGas   0    FossilFuels        FossilGas NaturalGas
#> 4  Biodiesel  15      Renewable        Bioenergy  Biodiesel

Colours are presentation and stay in energypal, which remains the editable source of the taxonomy’s names, labels and aliases; carriers is a snapshot of it. When a figure needs colours, join them from energypal by member name – the article Fuels, regions and months on the package site does so.

Country-specific values

The IPCC defaults are global. A calorific value for hard coal in Poland is the same attribute at the same fuel with a different region – a second dimension, not a deeper frame. That belongs to a scale_product() of the fuel scale and a GeoScale from geoscales, with the regional values attached as their own source; it is not built in this version.
